beats.say: This week RISE Changes learned to check its own work.
Every failure seen in a real run is now a mechanical check. Each check answers with a sentence the model can repair from.
A figure's labels are held to five rules: no overlap, no crossing a shape, none outside the figure, none too small on a phone, and enough contrast.
A browser then draws each figure at phone size and at desktop size, and measures every label again.
The composer's words are checked for talk about process, and each run's first pass is scored and shown as one line.
The connector now logs one count line for each admitted Current. It holds rule ids and counts only, never anyone's words, and its answers are exactly as before.
Measured on the owner's machine, the slowest worst-case Current took 4.2 milliseconds.
RISE now draws its own figures with a figure kit: bars, flows, columns and stacks.
Every label is measured before drawing, so labels cannot collide. A label that does not fit is refused, never shrunk.
Each beat now also carries the numbers of the pull requests it speaks about. That fixes a miss in how sources were written.
A picture now sits on the beat that speaks of it. A picture that cites a change its beat does not speak of is refused.
Sparse figures are refused too. A picture must show something the words alone do not.
A change that no beat speaks of is now left out of the reading, instead of being repaired. It no longer costs the first pass.
A picture now ends where its beats move on, and the reading returns to RISE's eye.
The page also says plainly why a change was left out: minor, skipped by the router, records only, over the 24-change limit, or the reading did not speak of it.
RISE's engines are now named only as the opening and the close. RISE places them on the first and last beat, and a scene that names an engine is refused.
Dependency changes now get an incremental review. Critical advisories in changed versions block, and license drift warns.
Published releases now have an experimental software bill of materials exporter, which attaches the unchanged CycloneDX response with its digests.
No release export has been generated yet.
